title: FRANK C6 — Clay-Native Unified Cognitive Substrate
owner_fixed_target: FRANK is Clay-native across 4B explicit symbolic cognition/output, memory, state, values/vector semantics, architecture, GWT, Hyperposition and internal semantic communication. Needle is the sole intentional non-Clay semantic subsystem.
core_findings: C6 changes C5's cross-language Reader ABI into a Clay-to-Clay View/Lowering Compiler; deterministic slicing/reduction/local handles/privilege typing/projection receipts still matter after model internalization.

The strongest target architecture is semantic monism with physical pluralism: one Clay semantic IR family can lower into model tokens, graph records, binary wire formats, vectors/tensors and native platform code without making all data literal text or forcing one database.

Full-model Clay adaptation should transcode retained pretrained competence into Clay rather than optimize target-language loss alone; external language-adaptation evidence makes catastrophic forgetting a primary risk.

ClayGraph becomes the target persistent explicit symbolic memory portion of the same cognitive substrate as the Clay-native 4B, but exact truth, semantic epochs, activation, selection integrity and conditional graph escalation remain distinct mechanisms.

Native model-memory alignment can compound efficiency and memory influence but can also compound graph poisoning/common-mode semantic errors; epistemic record types and selector provenance become more important.

Clay-native values/vectors should use semantic basis/axis/unit/time/provenance/version headers with efficient binary/tensor payloads; text-only vectorization is rejected as a universal physical representation.

Needle is retained as the sole non-Clay semantic reflex/classifier. It produces an immutable Clay route certificate; model/memory cannot silently rewrite route class and Needle still does not mint effect authority.
All-Clay GWT retains causal stage orthogonality: graph prior, candidate formation, workspace selection/ignition, Clay view/model uptake and re-entry remain separately intervenable.
Self-description in Clay does not grant self-authority: owner/capability contracts can be represented in Clay while deterministic compiled enforcement protects privileged mutation paths.
Clay-native recurrence/continuity is not emergence evidence; E-CERT2 or successor remains required.
external_evidence_highlights: ACL 2025 language adaptation: target-language validation perplexity can hide early catastrophic forgetting; curriculum/EMA are relevant mitigation candidates.

ACL 2026 Source-Shielded Updates: full fine-tuning produced substantially larger source-task degradation in tested 7B/13B language-adaptation settings; selective freezing is a scientific baseline, not the C6 target.
IRCoder: continued causal training on source/LLVM-IR pairs taught shared IR constructs to 1.1B–7.3B models and improved multiple code tasks, supporting learned machine IR plausibility.
Learn2Zinc: rare DSL syntax can be taught to small models while semantic solution accuracy remains much lower, supporting separate Clay syntax/execution metrics.
Instruction Hierarchy and 2026 graph-memory poisoning work support explicit privilege/epistemic typing and memory-level integrity controls.
MLIR-style dialect/lowering architecture is an engineering analogue for one semantic IR family with multiple optimized representations.
